title: Base graphics, coordinates and owned devices
outcome: Construct a labeled base-R graphic and manage an explicitly owned file device without confusing drawing with browser delivery.
mechanism:
Base graphics draws into the active graphics device. A high-level plot establishes a coordinate system and axes, while lower-level functions such as points, lines, segments and text add marks to that existing plot. Calling another high-level plot usually starts a new plot rather than adding a layer to the current one.

The coordinate system should match the analytic meaning. A scatterplot shows paired observations; connecting points with lines introduces an order relationship. If rows are not sorted by the intended time or predictor, a line can imply transitions that the data do not support. Label axes with quantities and units rather than relying on familiar-looking numbers.

A graphics device is an output target, such as the classroom's captured PNG device or an explicitly opened file. Opening a PNG device and then calling plot is different from merely constructing an object that describes a plot. Closing the owned device flushes its output, after which the file can be inspected. A file existing before closure may not yet represent a complete image.

Device ownership matters in reusable code. A helper should close only the device it opened and clean up only its own temporary files. Closing every device or deleting a broad output directory can interfere with the surrounding classroom or another analysis. Use scoped cleanup and preserve the caller's device when returning.

The default classroom captures base graphics separately from the numerical transcript. The file-device example demonstrates actual PNG creation and signature validation in an owned temporary path. It does not by itself prove that a browser displayed the image, that every text label is readable at the final size, or that a printed export meets publication requirements. Those are additional visual checks.

vocabulary.definition: The active destination for graphical drawing commands.
A call establishing a new plot and coordinate system.
Marks added to the current plot without replacing its coordinate system.
A file or device created by the current operation and cleaned up within that scope.

anatomy: Use plot to establish axes and labels, then points or abline to add marks in the same coordinates. xlim/ylim define the intended range; xaxs="i" and yaxs="i" remove default range expansion when exact coordinate checks are needed. For a file, call grDevices::png, retain dev.cur(), draw, then dev.off for that owned device before reading its bytes.

worked_examples.title: A labeled plot with an overlay
worked_examples.code:
d <- data.frame(x = 0:4, y = c(0, 2, 4, 6, 8))
plot(d$x, d$y, xlim = c(0, 4), ylim = c(0, 8), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i", xlab = "Input value", ylab = "Response value", pch = 16, main = "Observed pairs and stated linear rule")
abline(a = 0, b = 2, col = "#1B5E20", lwd = 2)
stopifnot(max(abs(par("usr") - c(0, 4, 0, 8))) < 1e-12)
stopifnot(all(d$y == 2 * d$x))
worked_examples.explanation: The line overlays the same coordinate system as the observations. The exact axis limits are checked without interpreting that software check as a visual readability review.
worked_examples.expected: One base graphic; coordinate limits 0/4/0/8 and the line through all five points.

worked_examples.title: Write and close an owned PNG
worked_examples.explanation: The function closes its device before reading the signature, then removes only its own tempfile. It returns evidence of file production, not a claim that an external viewer rendered it.
worked_examples.expected: A nonempty PNG with the expected signature, followed by owned cleanup.

exercises.prompt: Draw the five paired observations with labeled axes.
exercises.hint: Use a high-level plot before overlays.
exercises.answer: A scatterplot establishes the coordinate system and identifies the measured quantities.

exercises.prompt: Overlay the rule y=2x without starting another plot.
exercises.hint: Use abline or lines in the current coordinates.
exercises.answer: The overlay shares the established axes and passes through the authored points.

exercises.prompt: Set and inspect exact limits 0:4 and 0:8.
exercises.hint: Disable range expansion for this coordinate check.
exercises.answer: With xaxs/yaxs set to i, par("usr") matches the four declared bounds.

exercises.prompt: Diagnose connecting unsorted rows in a time-series line.
exercises.hint: Identify which order the line follows.
exercises.answer: lines follows supplied order. Sort by the declared time variable or use an appropriate grouping/order rule before implying a trajectory.

exercises.prompt: Create, close and validate an owned PNG tempfile.
exercises.hint: Flush the device before reading bytes.
exercises.answer: The file has a valid PNG signature and is removed by scoped cleanup; unrelated devices remain owned by their callers.
exercises.expected: Actual file evidence and scoped cleanup.

exercises.prompt: Distinguish numerical, file and browser evidence for the graphic.
exercises.hint: Name what each check actually observes.
exercises.answer: Data assertions check values, signature checks file structure, and a browser inspection checks delivery/readability. None automatically substitutes for the others.

reference:
d <- data.frame(x = 0:4, y = 2 * (0:4))
plot(d$x, d$y, xlim = c(0, 4), ylim = c(0, 8), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i", pch = 16, xlab = "Input value", ylab = "Response value", main = "Pairs and linear rule")
abline(a = 0, b = 2, col = "#1B5E20", lwd = 2)
stopifnot(max(abs(par("usr") - c(0, 4, 0, 8))) < 1e-12, all(d$y == 2 * d$x))
unsorted <- data.frame(time = c(3, 1, 2), value = c(30, 10, 20))
ordered <- unsorted[order(unsorted$time), ]
stopifnot(identical(ordered$time, c(1, 2, 3)), identical(ordered$value, c(10, 20, 30)))
owned_png <- function() {
  path <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  grDevices::png(path, width = 500, height = 350, type = "cairo")
  owned <- dev.cur()
  on.exit(
    {
      if (dev.cur() == owned) dev.off(); unlink(path)
    },
    add = TRUE
  )
  plot(1:3, c(2, 1, 4), pch = 16, xlab = "Observation", ylab = "Value")
  dev.off()
  stopifnot(identical(readBin(path, "raw", n = 8), as.raw(c(137, 80, 78, 71, 13, 10, 26, 10))))
  stopifnot(file.info(path)$size > 0)
  path
}
removed <- owned_png()
stopifnot(!file.exists(removed))
cat("r-051 reference checks passed\n")
solution_explanation:
The reference produces at most two graphics: one in the caller's active device and one in an owned temporary PNG device. It checks the underlying pairs and explicit coordinate range, then separately validates file structure and cleanup.

The row-order example is numerical so the cause of a misleading connected line is inspectable without relying on an image. Actual classroom delivery and readability still require the browser/figure acceptance workflow; a successful Rscript exit does not establish those observations.
